blocks.text: To manufacture H₂SO₄, sulphur trioxide gas is produced from SO₂ and O₂, in a reversible process.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: For this equation the book itself gives ΔH° = −198 kJ (topic 8.14), −197 kJ mol⁻¹ (Quick Check 8.6 table) and −197.9 kJ mol⁻¹ (exercise, MCQ II). −97.9 kJ mol⁻¹ is not the value for 2 mol SO₃; read ΔH = −197.9 kJ mol⁻¹. The reaction is exothermic either way.

According to Le-Chatelier’s principle, a high pressure and low temperature are the essential conditions to have better yield of SO₃. At low temperature, the equilibrium constant for the formation of SO₃ is large, but equilibrium is achieved very slowly. As the temperature is raised, the rate increases but the yield of SO₃ drops off.
